title: NFL Rushing + Receiving Live-Game Repair — Step 3 Rushing Live Repair
problem: Rushing Yards still failed closed during an actual in-progress NFL game after the shared Step-2 LIVE identity bridge because one or more athlete IDs returned by the deployed Kyre Sports API were absent from the current-roster allowlist used by the render-time guard.
root_cause: The public Rushing API and Streamlit identity guard were operating from different deployment generations. Streamlit main contained the Step-2 LIVE bridge, while kyre-sports-api remained manually deployed from Render branch mlb-step17b-shared-host-cert at commit 905868dbf166fd56eeac34ff2a3bfa6715c1e875 with auto-deploy off. The older API could return a live-game player set containing an athlete no longer present in the current ESPN roster allowlist. Rushing V16 passed the whole payload to the shared all-or-nothing guard, so one stale API athlete ID made the entire page fail closed.
patch: Rushing V16 only: during an already-verified LIVE identity bridge, compare otherwise well-formed API athlete IDs with the same current-roster allowlist the frozen shared guard uses, remove only IDs absent from that allowlist, and then run the frozen shared guard over the reconciled payload using the same cached snapshot/roster evidence. Malformed/team-mismatched rows remain visible to the guard and still fail closed. Pregame/final behavior, Receiving, shared Step-2 gate, router, model, projection, probability, ranking, sportsbook, staking, wagering, Render deployment and API 2 remain unchanged.
